item.title: Free Dental Clinics Near Me: How to Find Free and Low-Cost Dental Care
item.description: A free or low-cost dental clinic near you is one of three kinds: a federally funded community health center that charges on a sliding scale by income, a public health department dental clinic, or a volunteer charity clinic. Find community health centers with HRSA's Find a Health Center search, then call to confirm eligibility, documents and cost before you go.

item.title: Dental School Clinic Near Me: Reduced-Fee Care From Supervised Students
item.description: A dental school clinic treats the public at reduced fees: dental students and residents provide care under the close supervision of licensed dentists, and dental hygiene programs offer supervised cleanings, X-rays and preventive care. Find accredited programs near you in the Commission on Dental Accreditation directory, and expect a screening visit first, longer appointments and several visits.

item.title: Assisted Living vs Memory Care vs a Senior Care Home in Tennessee
item.description: In Tennessee, assisted living means a licensed Assisted-Care Living Facility; a smaller senior care home is usually a licensed Residential Home for the Aged; memory care is not a separate license but dementia care delivered inside one of them. All three are licensed by the Tennessee Health Facilities Commission.

item.title: Assisted Living Cost in Memphis: Germantown vs Collierville vs Bartlett vs Southaven
item.description: Assisted living in Tennessee had a 2025 median private-pay cost of $67,140 a year, about $5,595 a month (CareScout 2025 Cost of Care Survey). No public survey publishes a separate figure for Germantown, Collierville, Bartlett or Southaven, so compare written quotes from communities in each city.

item.title: Moving a Parent From Memphis to Olive Branch or Southaven: Cross-State Checklist
item.description: Moving a parent from Memphis to an assisted living community in Olive Branch or Southaven means changing states: a different licensing body (the Mississippi State Department of Health), a different Medicaid program (Mississippi's Assisted Living Waiver instead of TennCare), and new records, address and benefit changes to file before move-in day.

item.title: TennCare CHOICES vs Mississippi Medicaid vs Private Pay for Assisted Living
item.description: TennCare CHOICES and Mississippi's Assisted Living Waiver both pay for assisted living services, not room and board, and only at communities that contract with them. Private pay covers everything and opens every door. In 2026 TennCare caps the room-and-board charge at $2,385.60 a month for CHOICES members.

item.title: West Tennessee vs East Arkansas Senior Living: Licensure and Placement Rules
item.description: West Tennessee and East Arkansas license senior living differently. Tennessee's Health Facilities Commission licenses assisted-care living facilities and residential homes for the aged; Arkansas's Office of Long Term Care licenses assisted living facilities at Level I or Level II, and Arkansas Medicaid's Living Choices program pays only in Level II.

item.title: VA Aid and Attendance for Assisted Living in Tennessee: Eligibility and Budget
item.description: VA Aid and Attendance is an increase to the VA pension for veterans and surviving spouses who need help with daily activities. From December 1, 2025, the maximum annual pension with Aid and Attendance is $29,093 for a veteran with no dependents and $34,488 with a spouse; the net worth limit is $163,699.

item.title: Hospital Discharge to Assisted Living in Memphis: What Discharge Planners Need From Families
item.description: When a parent leaves Baptist, Methodist, Saint Francis or Regional One for assisted living, the hospital's discharge planner must evaluate post-discharge needs and send necessary medical information to the receiving community. Families supply the decision: which community, its acceptance, payment, and signed documents, often within a day or two.

item.title: Private Pay vs Medicaid Beds: Why Some Memphis Communities Don't Take TennCare
item.description: Some Memphis assisted living communities don't take TennCare CHOICES because TennCare caps what they can collect: in 2026, at most $3,883.37 a month for a CHOICES member, services and room and board combined. Tennessee's 2025 private-pay median is about $5,595 a month, so many communities limit or decline CHOICES beds.

item.title: ADHD evaluation vs neuropsychological evaluation
item.description: An ADHD evaluation answers a focused diagnostic question; a neuropsychological evaluation is broader and may be useful when learning, memory, neurological, or complex differential questions are also present. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to neuroevalguides.com for the complete canonical next step.

item.title: Civil surgeon vs panel physician
item.description: Use a civil surgeon for USCIS adjustment-of-status medical exams in the United States; panel physicians handle immigration medical exams abroad under Department of State processes. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to uscisexam.com for the complete canonical next step.

item.title: Comparative negligence vs contributory negligence
item.description: Comparative negligence reduces recovery according to assigned fault under state rules; contributory-negligence systems can bar recovery when the claimant is legally at fault, subject to jurisdiction-specific exceptions. Compare the categories, verify the current source, and continue to theaccidentguides.com for the complete canonical next step.
